# PR Review Sweep

A sweep reviews code that is **already merged**. Nothing here is a change under
review: there is no diff, no author to answer and no merge to gate. It produces
defects already in the tree, each tagged **Pre-existing**, so readers can tell
nobody introduced them today (REQ-021, AC-021-1).

It runs **when it is invoked**, and only then (AC-021-2, Constitution Rule 4).
This skill holds no timer, no schedule, no watcher and no background poll, and
ensemble's own `.github/workflows` carry no `schedule:` trigger. Recurrence is
the **host repository's** job (a workflow it owns) or **Foreman's**. The recommended cadence is **weekly**,
and a sweep starts with the sensitive areas (REQ-003).

This skill owns editable prose only (Rule 8). Every judgement that grades a
claim -- sensitivity, rules, depth, slice coverage, ledger validity, the
verification vote -- is made by `pr-review-cli.js` (Rule 7), the same binaries
`pr-review-cycle` uses, so a sweep finding meets the standard a PR finding does.
Payload shapes, the inputs table and report contents: `reference/sweep-details.md`.

---

## Inputs

`SCOPE` (paths, directories or globs, `['.']` for everything; empty or
unreadable is an error, never "everything by default"), `SWEEP_SHA` (a full 40-
or 64-hex commit id, never a bare ref; guidance is read from THIS commit,
REQ-024), `REQUESTED_BY` (recorded only), optional `TIER` (absent means `high`),
optional `MAX_PATHS` (a truncated sweep is never reported as complete), optional
`TEST_COMMAND` (reproduction notes; a sweep runs no tests). Table: reference.

## Outputs

Exactly one of:

- **`SWEEP_COMPLETE`** -- paths examined, slices reviewed, verified findings
  (all tagged Pre-existing) and what was left for a next run.
- **`SWEEP_BLOCKED`** -- what could not be read or graded, and no findings list.
  A sweep that could not resolve its scope, guidance or verification reports
  that; it never reports a clean repository.

A sweep never writes code, never opens a PR, never pushes and never resolves
anybody's review thread. It reports.

---

## Resolve the CLI

Resolve `PR_REVIEW_CLI` per the tool-path-resolution skill
(`packages/development/skills/tool-path-resolution/SKILL.md`) for
`packages/development/lib/pr-review-cli.js`. If none of the 4 tiers resolve OR
`which node` fails: print `ERROR: Node.js and the PR review CLI
(lib/pr-review-cli.js) are required for deterministic review grading.` and HALT.

Invoke subcommands as in `pr-review-cycle`: `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI"
<subcommand>`, one JSON payload on stdin, one JSON object on stdout. A non-zero
exit is `SWEEP_BLOCKED` naming the CLI error -- never a retry with guessed input.

---

## Algorithm

### Step 1 -- Resolve what will be swept

List the files under `SCOPE` at `SWEEP_SHA` from that commit's tree listing
(with sizes): the sweep set. A path absent at `SWEEP_SHA` is reported as not
found, never silently dropped.

### Step 2 -- Resolve guidance from the swept commit (CLI `policy`, `rules`, `paths`)

Read the guidance a PR review reads, from `SWEEP_SHA`: `policy` with `text` set
to the content of `REVIEW.md` at `SWEEP_SHA` (`null` when none -- the CLI then
answers with the strict defaults, which is not the same as no policy); `rules`
over the sweep set with every `REVIEW.md` at `SWEEP_SHA` (`baseSha` and
`sourceSha` both `SWEEP_SHA`); and `paths` with `declaration`
is `{ sourceSha: <SWEEP_SHA>, sensitive, high }` (from the policy) and
CODEOWNERS from `SWEEP_SHA`. Shapes: reference, "Step 2".

The `paths` result's `sensitive` and `high` lists order Step 3. A guidance call
that answers `ok:false` is `SWEEP_BLOCKED`: a sweep under unreadable guidance is
not a sweep of this repository.

### Step 3 -- Sensitive areas first (REQ-003, AC-021-2)

Sweep in this order, and report each finding's band:

1. every path in `paths.high`;
2. every path in `paths.sensitive` not already swept;
3. everything else in the sweep set.

When `MAX_PATHS` truncates the run, it truncates from the **end** of that
order: sensitive bands are swept first and completely, and the report names the
paths left. A sweep that skipped a sensitive path reports
itself as incomplete, whatever else it found.

### Step 4 -- Depth and slices (CLI `depth`, `slices`)

Run `depth` with `TIER`, the policy's bounds override and the planned
`{ reviewers, verifiers }`. `violations` is binding
exactly as it is in `pr-review-cycle`: re-plan and call again until it is
empty, and never dispatch a plan the CLI refused.

Run `slices` over the sweep set (`lines` per file; no diff) with the rules and
sensitive areas, the policy's threshold and `depth`'s `mode`; its `reviewerAssignments`
are the plan. Then re-run it with `reviewedBy` and `changedPaths` to prove coverage:
an `uncovered` or `underReviewed` path is reported as unswept, never as clean. Shapes: reference, "Step 4".

### Step 5 -- Review with the same reviewers (fresh context, read-only)

Dispatch one reviewer per `reviewerAssignments` entry -- at Standard or Deep **at least two** per slice,
each a **fresh-context, read-only** subagent under its `lens` -- over the sweep set, slice by
slice, in the Step 3 order. Each gets only its slice's whole files at
`SWEEP_SHA`, the rules `applied` with policy and sensitivity facts, and the
repository guidance -- never the authoring conversation, this session or an
issue tracker's opinion. No reviewer edits, stages, commits or pushes anything.

Record every candidate as a ledger entry exactly as `pr-review-cycle` Step 3
does, with **`severity` set to `Pre-existing` on every one of them**
(AC-021-1) and a **valid `disposition`**, one of `fix|duplicate|not-applicable|deferred|adjudicate|resolved`
(a sweep never fixes: use `deferred` with a `reason` naming the follow-up,
unless marked `duplicate` or `not-applicable`). `Pre-existing` is the third word of the
ledger's closed severity set (`Important`, `Nit`, `Pre-existing`), but only
`recordRound` normalises it: run the batch through
`node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" ledger` with `action: 'recordRound'` and
`{ ledger: [], incoming: <candidates>, round: 1 }`; the entries in its
`findings` come back with `preExisting: true`, and every consumer reads the
same fact. It is set because the code was swept, never because a reviewer
judged a defect old.

Then check `findings` with `action: 'validate'`; a finding missing a required
field or with an invalid disposition is completed, never dropped, and one
without `preExisting: true` was not tagged -- fix its severity and run
`recordRound` again before reporting. Carry the reviewer's own severity
judgement in the report, `failureMode` and `evidence` (reference, "Step 5").

Because `Pre-existing` findings never block a merge gate and are not
`isActionable` work on somebody else's PR, a sweep can never stop anybody's PR:
it informs, and the repository decides what to fix.

### Step 6 -- Verify before anything is reported (CLI `votes`)

Candidates are not findings until verified, by the same rule and thresholds as
a PR review. Run `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" votes` with
`{ findings, depth, expectedVerifiers, verificationCapability }`: the depth's
verifiers (Standard 3, Deep 5), each a fresh-context subagent, and **never the
reviewer that raised the finding**. Report exactly `presented[]` -- `present`,
`disputed` and `unverified` -- with each finding's `authorLabel` verbatim. A
`filtered` finding stays in the ledger with its tally and is not reported as
something to fix.

On a runtime with no subagents, degrade exactly as `pr-review-cycle` does: one
single-pass review, `verificationCapability: false`, every finding
`unverified` / `no-subagent-capability`, and the reduced-review notice. A reduced sweep is never reported as a verified one.

### Step 7 -- Report

Report in one place the requester, `SWEEP_SHA`, scope, paths examined in band
order, slices reviewed, every verified finding (band, path:line, severity,
`authorLabel`, **Pre-existing** tag), what was left for the next run, and the
reduced-review notice when verification did not run (reference, "Step 7").

Findings are **not** filed as PRs, commits or issues by this skill; the
maintainer or host automation decides what becomes work.

---

## Recurrence belongs to the host repository (AC-021-2)

This skill runs once per invocation and never schedules itself.
`/ensemble-init-project` offers a weekly workflow template -- **opt-in, never
written unless the user asks for it** -- the host's file once it lands; the
**core review path needs no new CI secret** (reference, "Recurrence").
Ensemble ships no `schedule:` trigger of its own (Rule 4).

---

## Safety rules

- A sweep reports; it never changes code, on any branch, including the one swept.
- Every sweep finding carries the `Pre-existing` severity, so the ledger
  records `preExisting: true` for it; untagged, it would read as a fresh
  regression and count as an open Important finding at the merge gate.
- Sensitive areas are swept first and completely; a truncated run names what it
  left and never reports itself as complete.
- Verification is not optional: an unverified candidate is reported as
  `unverified`, never as a defect the repository must fix, and never dropped.
- Guidance is the swept commit's copy, read from `SWEEP_SHA` itself, never the
  working tree's.
- This skill never schedules, polls, waits for a trigger or recovers
  unattended. It is invoked, it runs, it reports, it ends.
